observations.text: SP, due to an incorrect power and pursuit-curve technique in converting A/C energy, did not maintain the tactical formation position as No2 during the navigation route. Line abreast deviation exceeded 30 degrees aft and lateral separation opened beyond 1000 feet from the briefed spacing. The IP directed the geometry of the correction and executed part of the repositioning, so position keeping was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to an unagreed division of lookout responsibility within the formation, did not execute clearing of the assigned responsibility airspace as No2 and lost visual contact with the Leader. Lateral separation opened beyond 1000 feet with an altitude split greater than 1000 feet high before the deviation was reported. The IP took the A/C to re-establish the tactical formation position, and deconfliction was not achieved without IP's assistance.

SP maintained the tactical formation position as No2 only after the IP's verbal indications, holding line abreast deviation at the 30 degree limit and lateral separation at 1000 feet. Deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, but no intervention on the controls was required. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of closure rate and timely corrections are expected to improve.

SP maintained the tactical formation position as No2 without verbal indications from the IP, applying the proper corrections to alleviate deviations from the briefed position. Line abreast deviation reached 20 degrees and lateral separation 750 feet during the tactical turns, both recognized early and corrected by the SP without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed clearing of the corresponding responsibility airspace and maintained the tactical formation position as No2 with accuracy and speed. Deviations remained within 10 degrees line abreast and 400 feet of lateral separation, with recovery headings within 10 degrees and entry/exit speed within 15 knots. A/C energy was exploited and converted correctly to hold position, with engine use showing consideration to the fuel reserve. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained the tactical formation position as No2 throughout all phases of flight with exceptional accuracy, the deviations in altitude, lateral separation and line abreast remaining negligible. All visual signals given by the Leader were correctly identified and executed comm-out, and recovery headings and entry/exit speeds were held with negligible error. Clearing of the corresponding responsibility airspace was continuous and engine handling showed consideration to the fuel reserve. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect energy management technique during the tactical turn, did not exploit and convert A/C energy in order to maintain position, allowing the sustained G to vary by more than 1.0 G from the briefed value. Lateral separation closed by more than 1000 feet from the briefed spacing and the recovery heading was missed by more than 30 degrees. The IP intervened on the controls to restore safe separation, and the maneuver was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to failure to make the knock-it-off call when the briefed parameters were exceeded, continued the tactical turn without applying corrections to alleviate the deviation from the tactical formation position. Altitude deviated more than 1000 feet high and line abreast deviation exceeded 30 degrees before the sequence was stopped. The IP directed the recovery and executed part of the maneuver, and the briefed parameters were re-established only with IP's assistance.

SP, due to a delayed and coarse power correction technique in the turns, did not timely apply the proper corrections to alleviate deviations from the tactical formation position. Line abreast deviation reached the 30 degree limit and entry/exit speed deviated by 30 knots, corrected only after the IP's verbal indications. Errors were recognized with delay, without any intervention on the controls.

SP, due to degraded situational awareness after the unplanned change of turn direction, did not maintain the assigned tactical formation position as No2 during the cross turn. Altitude deviated to 1000 feet high and the recovery heading was missed by 30 degrees, both corrected with delay after the IP's verbal indications. The SP retained control of the A/C throughout, but recognition of the deviations was consistently late.

SP maintained the tactical formation position as No2 within the desired standards; however, line abreast deviation twice reached 20 degrees and lateral separation opened to 800 feet during the tactical turns. All deviations were recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner, without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in energy conversion and earlier corrections are expected to improve.

SP executed the position keeping as No2 with accuracy and speed, correctly exploiting and converting A/C energy in every tactical turn. Line abreast deviation remained within 10 degrees, lateral separation within 500 feet and recovery headings within 10 degrees, with entry/exit speed held within 15 knots. Clearing of the corresponding responsibility airspace was executed throughout and no verbal indication from the IP was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained the tactical formation position as No2 with exceptional accuracy during all phases of flight, with negligible deviations in altitude, lateral separation and line abreast. Sustained G in the turns was held with negligible variation from the briefed value and all visual signals given by the Leader were executed without prompting. Engine handling showed consideration to the fuel reserve over the whole navigation route. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect turn rate and power technique as No2, did not roll out in the tactical formation position after the delay 90 turn. Lateral separation opened beyond 1000 feet, the recovery heading was missed by more than 30 degrees and altitude deviated more than 500 feet low. The IP took the A/C and repositioned the formation, so the maneuver was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to complacency on a maneuver flown repeatedly without incident, did not execute clearing of the corresponding responsibility airspace before the tactical turn and did not monitor the Leader's aspect. Line abreast deviation exceeded 30 degrees and lateral separation closed by more than 1000 feet from the briefed spacing before the deviation was noticed. The IP intervened on the controls to restore safe separation. The tactical formation position was re-established only under IP's direction.

SP, due to a non-standardized correction technique for closure and aspect, did not timely apply the proper corrections to alleviate deviations from the tactical formation position. Lateral separation reached the 1000 feet limit and the sustained G varied by 1.0 G from the briefed value, corrected only after the IP's verbal indications. Errors were recognized and corrected with delay, without intervention on the controls.

SP, due to failure to shed a secondary task when workload increased on the navigation leg, did not maintain the tactical formation position as No2 during the in place turn. Altitude deviated to 1000 feet high and entry/exit speed by 30 knots, both corrected only after the IP's verbal indications. The IP did not intervene on the controls, but recognition of the deviations was consistently delayed.

SP, due to a coarse power technique during the energy conversion in the turn, did not hold the briefed sustained G, with the result of a 0.8 G variation and an altitude deviation of 400 feet low. The deviation from the tactical formation position was recognized early and corrected by the SP in a timely manner, without IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction from the primary visual scan by an unrelated switch action, did not hold the line abreast reference during the tactical turn, with the result that line abreast deviation reached 20 degrees and lateral separation 800 feet. The deviations were recognized early and corrected by the SP without IP's intervention, and clearing of the corresponding responsibility airspace was resumed immediately.

SP maintained the tactical formation position as No2 within the desired standards, with line abreast deviation within 10 degrees and lateral separation within 500 feet. However, the corrections after the delay 45 turns were repeatedly applied late in the roll-out and the recovery heading twice settled at the 10 degree limit. Marginal performance for the Training Section - anticipation of the roll-out reference and smoother energy conversion are expected to improve.

SP maintained the tactical formation position as No2 with exceptional accuracy throughout the navigation route, the deviations in altitude, lateral separation, line abreast and recovery heading remaining negligible. Clearing of the corresponding responsibility airspace was continuous, all visual signals given by the Leader were executed comm-out without prompting, and engine handling showed consideration to the fuel reserve. Performance exceeded the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
